item.title: 1991: Cal Ripken Jr. Wins AL MVP, Home Run Derby and All-Star MVP
item.description: Baltimore Orioles' Cal Ripken Jr. was named the American League MVP, thus became the first player to win the All-Star Home Run Derby, the All-Star Game MVP and the AL MVP in the same season. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2025: Bart Shirley, 85, Infielder for Dodgers and Mets
item.description: Bart Shirley, 85, Infielder from 1964–72 for the Dodgers and Mets in MLB and the Dragons in NPB.

item.title: 2021: Rangers Sign Woodward to Contract Extension Through 2023
item.description: On November 19, 2021, the Rangers signed Woodward to a contract extension through the 2023 season, with a club option for 2024. Photo: TonyTheTiger (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2021: Guardians Add Morris to 40-Man Roster
item.description: The newly named Cleveland Guardians selected Morris to their 40-man roster on November 19, 2021.

item.title: 2021: Cleveland Indians Rename Themselves Cleveland Guardians
item.description: The Cleveland Indians officially rename their team to become the Cleveland Guardians.

item.title: 2018: Yankees Acquire James Paxton From Mariners
item.description: The New York Yankees acquire left-handed pitcher James Paxton from the Seattle Mariners in exchange for pitchers Justus Sheffield and Erik Swanson and outfielder Don Thompson-Williams. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Marlins Sign Giancarlo Stanton to Record $325 Million Deal
item.description: The Miami Marlins officially announce the signing of Giancarlo Stanton to a record-setting 13-year, $325 million contract that includes a full no-trade clause and an opt-out provision after the sixth season. Stanton agrees to a heavily backloaded contract structure in order to leave the front office with flexibility to add significant pieces in order to contend in the immediate future. Photo: Jeffrey Hayes (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2012: Bautista Signs With Miami Marlins as International Free Agent
item.description: Bautista signed with the Miami Marlins as an international free agent on November 19, 2012.

item.title: 2009: Diamondbacks Acquire Heilman for Scott Maine and Ryne White
item.description: On November 19, 2009, Heilman was acquired by the Diamondbacks, in return for Scott Maine and Ryne White. Photo: Mark Winograd (Transfered by Maurilbert/Original uploaded by (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2007: Alex Rodriguez Wins Third Career AL MVP, Days After Yankees Deal
item.description: Just four days after agreeing to his new contract with the New York Yankees, Alex Rodriguez wins his 3rd career AL Most Valuable Player Award. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2006: Cubs Sign Alfonso Soriano to 8-Year, $136 Million Deal
item.description: The Chicago Cubs reportedly sign free agent Outfielder/Second Baseman Alfonso Soriano to an 8-year, $136 million deal. The signing is the largest in Cubs' history. Photo: Jauerback (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2004: Brian Traxler, 37, First Baseman for 1990 Dodgers
item.description: Brian Traxler, 37, first baseman for the 1990 Los Angeles Dodgers.

item.title: 1993: Dodgers Acquire DeShields for Prospect Pedro Martínez
item.description: On November 19, 1993, DeShields was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers for then-prospect Pedro Martínez. Photo: Joel Dinda (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1993: Howard Johnson Signs With Rockies, First Free Agent to Switch Teams
item.description: Howard Johnson who would turn 33 at the end of the month becomes the first free agent to sign with another team this off-season when he agreed to a one-year deal worth $2,100,000 to play for the Colorado Rockies. the switch-hitting slugger who led the National League in homers and RBIs two years ago with the New York Mets, has seen his production drop in recent seasons, primarily due to injuries. Photo: Wknight94 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1990: Barry Bonds Wins First NL MVP With Pittsburgh Pirates
item.description: Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder Barry Bonds won his first National League MVP.

item.title: 1988: Hubbell Suffers Stroke, Crashes Car Into Lamppost in Mesa
item.description: Hubbell suffered a stroke while driving near his home in Mesa, Arizona, on November 19, 1988, that caused him to lose control of his car and crash into a lamppost. Photo: AP (Public domain).

item.title: 1986: Mike Schmidt Wins Third NL MVP, Joins Musial and Campanella
item.description: Philadelphia Phillies third baseman Mike Schmidt wins the National League MVP Award, joining Stan Musial and Roy Campanella as the only three-time NL winners. Schmidt led his league with 37 home runs and 119 RBI while hitting a .290 average. Schmidt earns 287 points and 15 of 24 first-place votes, while Glenn Davis is the runner-up (231, six). Photo: Squelle (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1975: Joe Morgan Named NL MVP, Wins 21 of 23 First-Place Votes
item.description: Joe Morgan of the Cincinnati Reds, who led his team to its first World Series title in 35 years, is named the National League's Most Valuable Player, winning 21 of 23 first-place votes. (The other two go to teammate Pete Rose.) Photo: John VanderHaagen ; crop: Fui in terra aliena (talk) 17:25, 4 October (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1968: Stan Bahnsen Named AL Rookie of the Year, 17-12 With Yankees
item.description: New York Yankees pitcher Stan Bahnsen, who posted a 17–12 record with 162 strikeouts and a 2.05 ERA, is named American League Rookie of the Year. With 17 of 20 first-place votes, Bahnsen easily outdistances outfielder Del Unser of the Washington Senators, who notches three votes.

item.title: 1963: Hank Bauer Signs One-Year Deal to Manage Baltimore Orioles
item.description: United States Marine Corps veteran and former New York Yankees outfielder Hank Bauer signs a one-year contract to manage the Baltimore Orioles. Bauer succeeds Billy Hitchcock, fired September 29, and is expected to bring greater discipline to the Orioles' culture.

item.title: 1962: Cardinals Send Don Cardwell, Julio Gotay to Pirates for Dick Groat
item.description: St. Louis Cardinals general manager Bing Devine sends hurler Don Cardwell (obtained in October) and shortstop Julio Gotay to the Pittsburgh Pirates for All-Star shortstop Dick Groat (the National League MVP for 1960) and reliever Diomedes Olivo. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1956: Phillies Trade Del Ennis to Cardinals for Bobby Morgan, Rip Repulski
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies trade veteran left-fielder Del Ennis to the St. Louis Cardinals for infielder Bobby Morgan and outfielder Rip Repulski. Native Philadelphian, three-time All-Star and former "Whiz Kid" Ennis has played 11 seasons and smashed 259 homers for the Phillies, but has fallen out of favor with his hometown fans. Photo: Peter Bond from Philadelphia, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1953: Roy Campanella Wins Second NL MVP, Capturing 17 of 24 Ballots
item.description: Roy Campanella, Brooklyn's Cooperstown-bound catcher, wins the second of what will be his three National League MVP Awards, capturing 17 of 24 first-place ballots. In an unusual pattern, Campanella will be named MVP every other year between 1951 and 1955. Photo: ベースボール・マガジン社（Baseball Magazine Co. Ltd) (Public domain).

item.title: 1940: Cardinals Purchase Contract of Right-Hander Tot Pressnell From Dodgers
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals purchase the contract of right-hander Tot Pressnell from the Brooklyn Dodgers.

item.title: 1930: John Russell, Pitcher for Brooklyn Robins and Chicago White Sox
item.description: John Russell, pitcher for the Brooklyn Robins and Chicago White Sox between 1917 and 1922.

item.title: 1884: NL President A. G. Mills Resigns, Nick Young Replaces Him
item.description: National League president A. G. Mills resigns and league secretary Nick Young replaces him. Photo: Unknown photographer (Public domain).
